tools.name: Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9)
tools.scoring: Each item 0 (not at all) to 3 (nearly every day); total 0-27
tools.thresholds: 5 mild, 10 moderate, 15 moderately severe, 20 severe. 10 or more = "yellow flag"; 15 or more = "red flag" (manual). Any positive answer on item 9 (thoughts of self-harm) needs follow-up.
tools.licence: Free. No permission needed to reproduce, translate, display or distribute (Pfizer statement on phqscreeners.com).
tools.quote: PHQ-9 scores of 5, 10, 15, and 20 represented mild, moderate, moderately severe, and severe depression, respectively.
tools.licence_quote: no permission is required to reproduce, translate, display or distribute them
tools.document_title: Kroenke K, Spitzer RL, Williams JB. The PHQ-9: validity of a brief depression severity measure. J Gen Intern Med 2001;16(9):606-13
tools.used_in_spaceflight: NOT FOUND (no public source found showing PHQ-9 use on ISS)
tools.suggested_actions: Recommendation (team design, not from source): under 10 self-help and recheck in 2 weeks; 10-14 tell the crew medical officer and send at next ground contact; 15 or more, or any item 9 answer above 0, tell the CMO now and flag the ground packet as emergency.
tools.plain: This asks 9 questions about your mood over the last 2 weeks. Answer each one honestly. A higher score means you should talk to someone.

tools.name: Patient Health Questionnaire-2 (PHQ-2)
tools.items: 2 items (low mood, loss of interest), past 2 weeks
tools.thresholds: 3 or more = positive screen; then give the full PHQ-9
tools.licence: Free. No permission needed to reproduce, translate, display or distribute (Pfizer statement on phqscreeners.com).
tools.quote: a PHQ-2 score > or =3 had a sensitivity of 83% and a specificity of 92% for major depression
tools.licence_quote: no permission is required to reproduce, translate, display or distribute them
tools.document_title: Kroenke K, Spitzer RL, Williams JB. The Patient Health Questionnaire-2: validity of a two-item depression screener. Med Care 2003;41(11):1284-92
tools.suggested_actions: Recommendation: use as a quick daily or weekly check; if 3 or more, open the PHQ-9.
tools.plain: Two quick mood questions. If your score is 3 or more, the app will ask a few more.

tools.name: Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7)
tools.thresholds: 5 mild, 10 moderate, 15 severe (manual). 10 or more = "yellow flag"; 15 or more = "red flag".
tools.licence: Free. No permission needed to reproduce, translate, display or distribute (Pfizer statement on phqscreeners.com).
tools.quote: cutpoints of 5, 10, and 15 represent mild, moderate, and severe levels of depressive, anxiety, and somatic symptoms
tools.licence_quote: no permission is required to reproduce, translate, display or distribute them
tools.document_title: PHQ and GAD-7 Instruction Manual (phqscreeners.com, Pfizer)
tools.suggested_actions: Recommendation: same levels as PHQ-9 (under 10 self-help; 10-14 tell CMO; 15 or more tell CMO now and flag ground).
tools.plain: Seven questions about worry and nerves over the last 2 weeks.
tools.notes: Original validation: Spitzer RL et al. Arch Intern Med 2006;166(10):1092-7, PMID 16717171: "A 7-item anxiety scale (GAD-7) had good reliability".

tools.name: Karolinska Sleepiness Scale (KSS)
tools.items: 1 item, sleepiness in the last 10 minutes
tools.scoring: 9-point scale: 1 extremely alert, 3 alert, 5 neither, 7 sleepy but no difficulty staying awake, 9 extremely sleepy, fighting sleep
tools.thresholds: NOT FOUND as a formal cut-off. Physiological sleepiness signs appeared only between "sleepy" and "extremely sleepy" (Akerstedt 1990).
tools.licence: Copyrighted by Torbjorn Akerstedt. Written consent needed to reproduce, duplicate or adapt.
tools.quote: Reproduction, duplication or adaptation without the written consent of Torbjörn Ǻkerstedt is strictly prohibited.
tools.licence_quote: Copyright © Torbjörn Ǻkerstedt, 1990. Reproduced with permission.
tools.document_title: Shahid A et al. (eds). STOP, THAT and One Hundred Other Sleep Scales, ch. 47 Karolinska Sleepiness Scale (Springer 2012)
tools.suggested_actions: Ask Akerstedt for permission before embedding (contact listed in chapter).
tools.plain: Pick one number from 1 to 9 for how sleepy you feel right now.
tools.notes: Validation: Akerstedt T, Gillberg M. Int J Neurosci 1990;52:29-37, PMID 2265922.

tools.name: Psychomotor Vigilance Test, 3-minute brief version (PVT-B); ISS "Reaction Self Test"
tools.items: About 3 minutes of reaction-time trials to a light; ISS version adds 2 minutes of questions
tools.scoring: Reaction time, lapses (missed or slow responses), false starts; ISS version gives 0-100% vs astronaut norms
tools.thresholds: NOT FOUND in abstracts checked (lapse cut-off for PVT-B is in the full paper)
tools.licence: PVT-B and Reaction Self Test software by Pulsar Informatics / University of Pennsylvania: licence NOT FOUND (company sells to government and private users). The PVT method itself is published. Free alternative: US Army PC-PVT is described as freely available.
tools.free_to_use_in_app: Unclear. Method yes; the NASA/Pulsar software no (licence NOT FOUND). Writing our own 3-minute PVT from the published method is likely OK but get a check.
tools.quote: Test provides feedback on performance level (0-100%) relative to astronaut norms.
tools.licence_quote: we previously developed the PC-PVT, a freely available software system analogous to the "gold-standard" PVT-192
tools.document_title: Dinges DF et al. Psychomotor Vigilance Self Test on ISS (Reaction Self Test on Expeditions 21 & 22), NTRS 20090029851
tools.suggested_actions: Recommendation: use as a fatigue aid. Compare to own baseline. Do not use as a medical diagnosis.
tools.plain: Watch the screen. Tap as fast as you can when the light appears. It takes 3 minutes.
tools.notes: PVT-B validation: Basner M, Mollicone D, Dinges DF. Acta Astronaut 2011;69:949-959, PMID 22025811: "we developed a modified brief 3-min version of the PVT (PVT-B)".

tools.name: Spaceflight Cognitive Assessment Tool for Windows (WinSCAT)
tools.thresholds: "Off-nominal" vs baseline, judged by crew surgeon (numeric cut-off NOT FOUND)
tools.licence: NASA operational tool; not publicly released (no public download or licence found)
tools.quote: WinSCAT (Space flight Cognitive Assessment Tool for Windows), which is an 11- to 15-minute computer-based cognitive screening test
tools.document_title: NASA HRP Evidence Report: Risk of Adverse Cognitive or Behavioral Conditions and Psychiatric Disorders (2016)
tools.used_in_spaceflight: Yes, monthly on ISS and after unexpected medical events
tools.suggested_actions: Source: off-nominal scores are reviewed in context before changing the work-rest schedule.
tools.plain: A short set of thinking tests on the computer. Your score is compared with your own earlier scores.

tools.name: Cognition test battery (NASA, Basner et al.)
tools.items: 10 brief tests, 15 versions each, covering several thinking skills
tools.scoring: Per-test scores vs normative astronaut-like data
tools.licence: NOT FOUND (no public licence terms found)
tools.quote: Cognition consists of 15 unique forms of 10 neuropsychological tests that cover a range of cognitive domains
tools.document_title: Basner M et al. Development and Validation of the Cognition Test Battery for Spaceflight. Aerosp Med Hum Perform 2015;86(11):942-52
tools.used_in_spaceflight: Developed for spaceflight (NASA BMed report calls it the next step beyond WinSCAT)
tools.plain: A set of short thinking games made for astronauts.

tools.name: Positive and Negative Affect Schedule (PANAS)
tools.thresholds: NOT FOUND (no clinical cut-offs; normative data only)
tools.licence: Copyright 1988 American Psychological Association. Research use is commonly described as allowed with citation; app embedding terms NOT FOUND, ask APA permissions.
tools.quote: we developed two 10-item mood scales that comprise the Positive and Negative Affect Schedule (PANAS)
tools.licence_quote: Copyright 1988 by the American Psychological Association, Inc.
tools.document_title: Watson D, Clark LA, Tellegen A. Development and validation of brief measures of positive and negative affect: the PANAS scales. J Pers Soc Psychol 1988;54(6):1063-70
tools.notes: PsyToolkit says: "It seems that PANAS can be used for research" (secondary, not a licence).

tools.name: Profile of Mood States, 2nd edition (POMS 2)
tools.items: NOT FOUND (item count not on publisher page fetched)
tools.licence: Commercial. Sold by Pearson (Qualification level B). Not free to embed.
tools.quote: Publication date: 2012 Age range: 13 through adult Qualification level: B
tools.document_title: Pearson Assessments: POMS 2 - Profile of Mood States Second Edition (Heuchert J, McNair DM)
tools.suggested_actions: Do not embed. Use PHQ-2/PHQ-9 and GAD-7 instead.
tools.plain: A paid mood test. Not used in this app.

action_levels.status: RECOMMENDATION by researcher, built from the cited cut-offs and ISS procedures. Not a NASA rule. Needs sign-off by a clinician on the team.

levels.when: PHQ-9 or GAD-7 under 10, PHQ-2 under 3, item 9 = 0, no warning signs
levels.do: Self-help (sleep, exercise, talk to family at next call), repeat check in 1-2 weeks.

levels.when: PHQ-9 or GAD-7 10-14, or a big drop from own baseline, or a crewmate notices warning signs
levels.do: Tell the crew medical officer (CMO). Add to next routine summary for the ground. Ask for a private conference at next contact.

levels.when: PHQ-9 or GAD-7 15 or more, any PHQ-9 item 9 answer above 0, or any behavioural emergency warning sign
levels.do: CMO stays with the crew member. Send an emergency packet. If no link (LOS, far side, conjunction), start the onboard emergency procedure first and call the surgeon when the link returns.
